subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary, or should hard skill isolation use a separate strict policy while `enabled:false` remains an eligibility and prompt-visibility toggle?
rationale: The code change crosses public skill semantics, filesystem reads, shell execution, sandbox behavior, UI wording, and security documentation; automation cannot choose that compatibility/security tradeoff safely.

options.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny rule for the skill directory across model exposure, direct skill invocation, read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, sandbox materialization, UI, docs, and tests.

options.title: Add strict isolation separately
options.body: Keep current `enabled:false` compatibility as an eligibility toggle and add an explicit operator-controlled strict policy for disabled-skill filesystem and exec denial.

options.title: Document current trust model
options.body: Leave enforcement to existing filesystem, sandbox, exec approval, and plugin governance controls while making the non-boundary semantics explicit in UI and docs.

recommendation.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny rule for the skill directory across model exposure, direct skill invocation, read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, sandbox materialization, UI, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a security/product boundary and Peter Steinberger has the strongest adjacent history in dangerous skill install hardening and current main ownership signals.
